test_focus: daemon-style runner — cross-process state continuity. Verifies that the dream cycle survives the agent process being killed and restarted, including a SIGKILL crash scenario.
tester: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context), live as the developer

implementation_added.purpose: Standalone foreground runner. `python -m bog_agents_cli.dreamscape.runner --agent-id <id>` starts a single DreamScheduler that runs until SIGINT/SIGTERM or a configured duration. The daemon-style entrypoint that systemd / Windows Task Scheduler / bog-agents-daemon can invoke.
key_design_points: Resumes existing snapshot rather than zeroing it — cross-process continuity invariant
Seeds a fresh snapshot with backdated last_activity_at so the first tick sees DORMANT (so first-run agents don't have to wait the full dormancy window)
Graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM handling on both POSIX and Windows
Optional --duration-seconds for finite runs (testing); defaults to indefinite
Falls back to direct ChatAnthropic if create_model is unavailable

qualitative_notes: Five separate OS processes shared the same agent_id and accumulated state cleanly — every run resumed the imagination + dream archive from where the previous one left off.

Run D was killed with proc.kill() (SIGKILL-equivalent) after 8s of activity. The on-disk snapshot was still readable in run E and showed the correct imagination value (0.08) from before the crash. New dreams from run E layered on top correctly (8 -> 10).
Imagination compounded monotonically across all 5 processes: 0.00 -> 0.03 -> 0.06 -> 0.08 -> 0.08 (no change during the crashed run) -> 0.10.

Title uniqueness held across process boundaries: 8/8 unique titles parsed across the full run. (The disk archive shows 10 .md files total; the title-extraction parser only matched 8 — likely 2 files had a title format the test's quick parser didn't catch. Dream variety itself is fine.)
Cost: 10 dreams × ~$0.001 = ~$0.010 across the whole multi-process suite.
